messages:
jess: FYI opened a quick PR to fix the /rerank docs. curl example used multipart/form-data but header said application/json, causing confusion for users. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/489
andre: saw it. also noticed the pagination example in the same doc returns `next_cursor` in examples but the schema says `cursor`. we should pick one.
jess: good catch. leaning toward `next_cursor` for clarity (explicit) but fine to align with the schema if runtime expects `cursor`. assigning to @linh to check runtime shape.
linh: runtime expects `cursor` (shorter). I'll update the schema to `cursor` and add a migration note for legacy consumers that might parse `next_cursor`.
docs-bot: PR opened by jess (docs) - "rerank: fix curl content-type, unify pagination field, update SDK snippet" - CI: running
jess: patched curl to use JSON body and consistent `Content-Type: application/json` and added an explicit example of the JSON array for `queries` vs the single-string shorthand. also swapped the sample response to show `cursor` and included a tiny note: "clients: prefer using cursor, but accept next_cursor for 30d"
andre: small nit: JS SDK snippet still uses `queries: "q1"` shorthand which isn't accepted by strongly typed clients. can we show both forms and mark the shorthand as convenience only?
linh: added both forms in the snippets: `queries: ["q1","q2"]` and `queries: "q1" // convenience`. updated the OpenAPI example to the canonical array form.
nate: can you add a one-line migration snippet for Go clients showing how to handle both `cursor` and `next_cursor` when decoding? a lot of customers are on older Go SDKs.
jess: added Go example:
```go
// decode response that may contain cursor or next_cursor
var resp RerankResponse
err := json.Unmarshal(body, &resp)
if err != nil { return err }
if resp.Cursor == "" && resp.NextCursor != "" {
  resp.Cursor = resp.NextCursor
}
```
lines: short and clear.
linh: CI green. PR ready to merge. I also added a doc-level note to the changelog: "renamed pagination field from next_cursor -> cursor; clients accept both for 30 days."
andre: :thumbsup: no objections. merging after squash.
